dedupe_keys.name: nankai trough megaquake working group material on lifeline and infrastructure countermeasures 2023

description: This Cabinet Office working group document reviews how lifeline operators are preparing for a Nankai Trough megaquake, together with the damage and restoration scenarios they plan against. It covers electricity, telecommunications, gas, water supply and sewerage, and fuel over 79 slides, restating the 2012 second damage estimate, for example up to about 27.1 million households losing power, around 90 per cent of customers in the Tokai, Kinki, Shikoku and parts of Kyushu regions, with power largely restored within about one to two weeks, alongside operators' countermeasures and issues such as cross-sector coordination to speed recovery. It was prepared by the Cabinet Office for the sixth meeting of the Nankai Trough Megaquake Countermeasures Working Group on 7 September 2023. The PDF is available free on the Cabinet Office disaster management website; no licence is named. Caveats: it is in Japanese, the scenarios are planning assumptions, not observations, and roads, rail, airports and ports were covered in a companion document. It supports multi-lifeline outage and restoration scenarios for earthquake and tsunami planning; a related record is the tsunami evacuation agent-based model.
name: Nankai Trough megaquake working group material on lifeline and infrastructure countermeasures (2023)
